en: Oṃ, salutation to Cit-bhairava!
Taking refuge in the ground of consciousness, take recourse in the manifestation of consciousness; do not wander in vain.

I bow to Śiva, who is indeed the supreme Bhairava of consciousness, the one, supremely nectarine, and intensely radiant; who, having devoured everything by means of his wheel of manifesting senses, remains as the All.
Though there may appear to be a distinction here between the object of praise, the praiser, and the act of praising, in reality, none of these exists.

Just as it imagines whatever form, so does this [world] become through its nature as consciousness. O Blessed One, I salute that which is Your reality— the mass of consciousness and bliss whose every distinction has dissolved, yet which is the self of all distinctions— and which, as Your likeness, bears Your very form.
Just as a line-drawing reveals a person and an assembly of letters reveals a collection of phonemes,
so too, O Supreme Self, does form manifest You who possess manifold aspects. Therein, having entered into You, whose nature is consciousness, one indeed becomes free from conceptual construction.
We shall reflect upon something, for reality is certainly not within the scope of conceptual construction.
Having established the Goddess of Speech as my own self-luminous light, having fashioned an offering of flowers from the objects [of perception],
and having first saluted the Guru who is the initial unfolding [of consciousness], I enter into the heart.

Reflecting upon Maheśvara, my own self, who is a single mass of consciousness from which the multitude of bonds has been washed away, I offer praise within this temple of the body. Victorious are the powers of the All-pervasive Lord, known as Cit (consciousness), Ānanda (bliss), Icchā (will), and Kriyā (action).
Assuming the form of a face through the division into subtle and gross, it is called Brahma and Muṇḍa;
the six limbs, beginning with the heart, have as their objects omniscience and the rest.
O Lord, this entire [universe] up to Sadāśiva serves as your seat in the form of a corpse.
O Lord, the reflective power (*vimarśa-śakti*) of You, whose body is supreme light, is the Goddess Parā;
all the goddesses beginning with Brāhmī are merely the expansion (*prasara*) of her alone.
Bearing within Yourself the lines of fire, water, nectar, poison, and so forth, You command this [universe].
Even though the universe appears contradictory, it does not contradict me, who am of the nature of Being-Consciousness.
This insubstantial collection of subjects, merged within the thread of consciousness, seems to show us, O Lord,
as if bearing a garland of severed heads that are the sense organs.
"Look, look! These snares of yours are ever uneven and cast outside"—thus you appear to us, speaking as if desiring to hold the entrails.
This very cloth of illusion, full of passion, has been cast upon this supreme sky.
Thus, O Lord, carrying the blood-stained elephant hide upon your head,
you manifest with the sword of inner power that pierces through cyclic existence;
for the most excellent heroes are those who have mastered the entire universe through the majesty of their own power.

"I am he who destroys the fear of worldly existence; I stand here as your protector, do not be afraid!"—thus you instruct us, O Master, by brandishing your sword. Time, though coiled within the noose of my own power, is rendered auspicious by me through my conscious form.
"By means of holding the noose, you, the Death of Death, manifest yourself to us.
"I myself shall withdraw this entire universe consisting of duality by my own power in order to destroy it"—
thus does the Supreme Bhairava make himself manifest to us through the holding of the goad.

By displaying the arrow mounted upon your bow, you pierce like a deer the deer that is the Cause (Hari), along with Brahmā, Viṣṇu, Rudra, Īśāna, and Sadāśiva, by means of Śakti. With your hand, which bestows boons, you gesture toward the granting of universal sovereignty.
Indeed, one who is established in the ultimate reality is never touched by the impurities of worldly existence.

And by means of fearlessness, which uproots the fears of cyclic existence, your nature— which has as its cause the favoring of the entire world— is constantly revealed, as if held in the palm of your hand.

This unequal head of Māyā, consisting of non-apprehension (akhyāti), has been severed here; thus you shine forth, bearing it as a shaven skull by me, who am composed of supreme awakening. The maintenance of the world, its essence entirely extracted, rests within me alone, who am a single mass of consciousness.
Thus, under the pretext of carrying a skull-topped staff (*khaṭvāṅga*) and a skeleton, you grant your command;
playing these fierce lutes, bells, and hand-drums, you direct this [message]:
"I stand here, listening to the sound divided into three distinct modes of existence."
Moreover, you constantly imitate the gods externally under the pretext of bearing the trident, [you who possess] the Great Power (Mahāśakti) beautiful with the three powers beginning with Parā;
[and you who possess] the triad of lower domains illuminated by your own powers beginning with Will (Icchā).
You alone bear your own supreme power, the six-spoked wheel composed of thunderbolts;
the entire world, subdued by my power, maintains all its various states of existence.
Thus, O Cit-bhairava, through the wielding of the staff, you manifest yourself to us.
O Īśāna, bearing a mallet and an axe whose forms imitate the [two] breasts of the Bindu,
you demonstrate your intent toward piercing, splitting, and shattering [the ego]. O Lord,
through the diversity of philosophical systems (*darśana*), you assume various modes of extraction (*āhṛti*).
You manifest your own abode, which consists of the supreme awakening of Bhairava, everywhere.
Within the midst of the Śākta-āṇḍa-khaṇḍa, I always drink all the essences of the universe;
you manifest this as if it were the blood of the guardians of hell within me.
O Mahākāla, you wear these two— arrogance and the knot of the heart— still intact with their tufts of hair,
like two budding lotuses; O treasury of awakening,
you thus emulate the primordial state, the source of the seed of the entire universe.
O Lord, because you sportfully display a *bījapūraka* fruit in the palm of your hand,
even though you possess the form of Bhairava, you hold a rosary (*akṣamālā*) in that very hand;
thereby, through the expansion of all the senses, you cause the universe to revolve within.
Adorned with bone ornaments, a garland of skulls, and ashes, and delighting in human blood, you, O Lord,
have declared that the universe is pure because it consists of Brahman.
To those who find delight in their own Self, are even these turbulent bubbles of sense-objects anything at all?
By manifesting the form of the supreme fire, you proclaim the eye of the forehead (the third eye) to be the burning fire of passion;
since you are always one whose aim is fixed within yet whose senses are ever-expanded,
you reveal yourself as having reached all states and being free from the stain of delusion.
O Lord, your state of being clothed only by space proclaims the unobscured nature of the Self;
how could the veil of *māyā* obscure those who consist of the Supreme Brahman, which is like the sun?
I am the ground of darkness for all [beings], including the sun and others, yet I am their destroyer.
With a body possessing the radiance of a stainless autumn sky, you thus manifest yourself. O Lord, since you, who consist of the Supreme Brahman, assume the form of Bhairava,
you, the knower of reality, demonstrate that one is liberated even while difference persists.
Surrounded by various garlands of cremation grounds and vetālas, you manifest within the sphere of objective cognition: "I am Citibhairava.
O Supreme Knower, within you alone resides the line of nectar consisting of the Supreme Power.
O Lord, You alone appear in our hearts as the very life of the worlds.
For You, whose body is the aggregate of all sounds, Your external retinue consists precisely of the eight groups of eight (the sixty-four deities),
appearing as Bhairavas, the Lords of the World, and others, through the distinctions of the supreme, the subtle, and so forth.
O Lord, Your form seals all this through the complete transference of Your own essential nature;
it gladdens the assembly of devotees by manifesting the joy of the ultimate goal and fullness;
it liberates from the web of bonds and dissolves all duality.

Because it seals the wealth of manifold consciousness, it is therefore called a *mudrā*. May this [mudrā], which serves as the means for entering the most excellent stage of the supreme reality (*paratattva*), clearly dwell within my heart through the expansion of true being; may this impurity be purified.

O Maheśa, those established in the sacrifice know that consciousness, which indeed flashes forth below as the universe— the very form of the glory of Śiva and Śakti— arises at every moment. Thus, O Bhairava of Consciousness, you who are the self of all beings, you always manifest within me.
Thus, everything from the sacrifice to the recitation has been accomplished without effort.
Thus ends the *Bhairavānukaraṇastotra*, composed by the illustrious Mahāmāheśvara Ācārya Śrī Kṣemarāja.
